claim: A 2011 intelligence memo emailed to Secretary of State Hillary Clinton by Sidney Blumenthal — later released from her private server — listed among the motives behind France's push to intervene in Libya that Muammar Gaddafi held large gold and silver reserves intended to establish a pan-African currency, which would have rivaled the French-backed CFA franc. NATO bombed Libya, Gaddafi was killed in October 2011, and the country fragmented. Fact-checkers caution there is little independent evidence Gaddafi actually planned a gold-backed currency, and the memo's sourcing was never disclosed.

sources.label: Vice — “Libyan Oil, Gold, and Qaddafi: The Strange Email Sidney Blumenthal Sent Hillary Clinton in 2011” (reproducing the released State Department email).
sources.quote: Gaddafi to use $7 billion in secret gold and silver to prop up a new African currency

sources.label: Africa Check — “Did Gaddafi plan to introduce an African currency backed by gold reserves? Maybe, but there's little evidence for this.”

notes: From @ojas_speaks reel DY0Oj5EpTHZ (“a leaked email to Hillary Clinton listed it as a motive for NATO's intervention”). Group B: the email's existence and content are verified (released from Clinton's server; reproduced by Vice, titled “France's client & Q's gold”), but whether Gaddafi truly planned a gold-backed pan-African currency — and whether it drove the intervention — is contested; Africa Check finds little independent evidence. The claim is framed as “the email lists it as a factor,” not as established motive. New anchor y2011-libya. The reel's further claim that NATO “bombed the civilian irrigation system that served 70% of the population” (the Great Man-Made River) is documented separately but not asserted in this record.
